topic: Country with the most lakes: Canada — ≈ 879,800 lakes above 0.1 sq km (HydroLAKES, Messager et al. 2016), about 62 % of the world's 1.42 million lakes of that size; Russia ≈ 201,200 second, USA ≈ 102,500; cause: Pleistocene glaciation; Great Bear (8th greatest) and Great Slave (10th greatest, deepest in North America) in the Northwest Territories
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Finland, the land of a thousand lakes, has the most lakes.
myths.reality: Finland has ~188,000 lakes of all sizes but Canada has about 880,000 lakes above the sailing-size threshold — more than every other country combined by that count.

hydrolakes.title: Messager et al. 2016 — Estimating the volume and age of water stored in global lakes using a geo-statistical approach (HydroLAKES)
hydrolakes.notes: 1.42 million lakes above 0.1 sq km worldwide; Canada ≈ 879,800 (≈ 62 %), Russia ≈ 201,200, USA ≈ 102,500

nrcan_lakes.title: Canada's lakes and freshwater
nrcan_lakes.notes: Canada has more lake surface than any other country; nearly 9 % of its territory is fresh water; Great Bear and Great Slave are its two greatest lakes

wiki_lakes.title: List of countries by number of lakes
wiki_lakes.notes: HydroLAKES counts: Canada 879,800; Russia 201,200; USA 102,500; Finland ~56,000 above 0.1 sq km

britannica_gbl.title: Great Bear Lake / Great Slave Lake
britannica_gbl.notes: Great Bear Lake 31,328 sq km, greatest entirely within Canada; Great Slave Lake 28,568 sq km, deepest in North America (614 m); both in the Northwest Territories

usgs_glaciation.title: Glaciers and glacial landforms — origin of lake basins
usgs_glaciation.notes: the Laurentide ice sheet covered nearly all of Canada; glacial scour and moraine damming created most of the lakes of the Canadian Shield

claims.text: Canada has the most lakes of any country: about 880,000 lakes above 0.1 sq km, more than the rest of the world combined (~62 % of 1.42 million).
vo: where are most of the world's lakes
canada. count every lake you could sail on, and canada holds more than the rest of the world combined

claims.text: Canada ≈ 879,800 lakes; Russia ≈ 201,200 (second); USA ≈ 102,500; Finland far fewer at that size threshold.
vo: nearly 880,000 lakes. russia, in second, has about 200,000. finland is not close

claims.text: The lakes are a legacy of the last ice age: the Laurentide ice sheet scoured the Canadian Shield and meltwater filled the hollows.
vo: why? ice. the last ice age scraped the land bare, and the meltwater filled every hollow it left

claims.text: Great Bear Lake and Great Slave Lake, in the Northwest Territories, are among the ten greatest lakes on Earth.
vo: great bear and great slave, far north, are giants, and most canadians have never seen them
